extracted.intended_audience: researchers, editors, journalists, and readers interested in scientific retractions and research integrity
extracted.subtask_description: Compiling and publishing a ranked list (leaderboard) of researchers by number of retractions, including methodology notes, inclusion rules, and periodic updates. Involves data verification, counting rules (e.g., authorship position, abstracts), and handling disputed or corrected counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: first_or_last_author_inclusion_rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Our rule is that only researchers who have been first or last authors of retracted papers are listed (middle authors are excluded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied inclusion policy: only count retractions where the individual is first or last author; middle-author-only cases are not included on the leaderboard (example: Emad Yahaghi excluded because he was only a middle author).

rubrics_metrics.name: count_abstracts_as_publications_when_investigation_calls_for_them
rubrics_metrics.description: We count abstracts as publications, as the investigations calling for 82 retractions did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal investigations treat abstracts/proceedings as publications subject to retraction, include them in an individual's tally; be explicit about including such items to explain discrepancies with other databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_of_web_of_science_with_editorial_judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: There are discrepancies between databases (e.g., Web of Science) and other accounts; we’ve used our judgment based on covering these cases to arrive at the highest numbers we could verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary data sources (e.g., Web of Science) can be used but expect inconsistencies; resolve discrepancies by manual verification and transparent editorial judgment, and document methodological choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: leaderboard_thresholds_for_top_listings
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bar — 25 — to be in the top 30 of our leaderboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply explicit thresholds for inclusion in ranked subsets (e.g., top 30 requires ≥25 retractions); state thresholds so users understand selection cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: authorship_responsibility_per_icmje
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship confers credit and has important academic, social, and financial implications. All persons designated as authors should qualify for authorship; each author should have participated sufficiently to take public responsibility for the content. By 2013 a fourth criterion was added: agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work and to identify which co-authors are responsible for specific parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ICMJE authorship criteria as a standard for assigning responsibility: (1) substantial contributions, (2) drafting/revising, (3) final approval, (4) accountability for all aspects; recognize that authorship implies both credit and accountability and that investigations should consider these criteria when assigning blame.

rubrics_metrics.name: recommendation_for_publication_audits_gpp3
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first time, 'auditing' appears in the Good Publication Practice guidelines (GPP3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publication audits (e.g., checking authorship criteria, disclosures, that authors had access to data) as a preventive measure; suggest a risk-based approach to audits to prevent misconduct and reduce retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid_group_level_inference_without_denominator_adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once it ventures into group-level interpretations (gender or otherwise) without denominator adjustment, mechanistic explanation, or cross-system context, it risks narrative overreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting aggregate patterns (e.g., by gender, nationality, ethnicity), avoid drawing causal or broad interpretations without appropriate denominators, normalization, and contextual caveats; explicitly state limits on inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: consider_retraction_ratio_normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps we should be more interested in someone's 'retraction ratio' – e.g., number of retractions as a percentage of their total output of papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize raw retraction counts by total publication output (or other denominators) to produce ratios that better reflect relative incidence rather than absolute counts; document numerator and denominator definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: consider_retraction_impact_factor
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be informative to have a retraction impact factor to rank order these fine fellows in a more meaningful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop metrics that weight retractions by the impact (citations, journal prestige, downstream influence) of the retracted papers so rankings reflect harm or reach as well as count.

rubrics_metrics.name: distinguish_culprit_vs_victim_based_on_investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The list should draw a distinction between a culprit and a victim. So, it should be open to any relevant update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use findings of formal investigations to annotate/tier entries (e.g., 'responsible', 'exonerated', 'undetermined'); update entries when new authoritative information becomes available to avoid mislabeling innocent co-authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: check_for_double_counting_retracted_article_vs_retraction_notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the Maryka Quik link it seems that you’ve counted both the retracted paper and the retraction letter. I actually count 8, not 16 retractions. You should give at least a quick check on all of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tallying retractions, ensure retraction notices or retraction letters are not double-counted alongside the original record; deduplicate entries and clearly define what constitutes a single 'retraction' event.

rubrics_metrics.name: track_journal_level_retraction_resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps you could have a leaderboard for journals: the number of fraudulent papers identified in formal investigations that remain unretracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and report journals that fail to retract papers identified as fraudulent in investigations; this helps hold journals accountable and highlights 'retraction-resistant' outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: include_institutional_affiliation_for_accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The list should also name the institution/organisation at which they’re employed. You know, the people that protect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current or relevant institutional affiliations for individuals on the list to improve transparency and enable institutional accountability; update affiliations as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: publish_last_update_date_and_versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Would it be informative if you insert last update date at the bottom of this post?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display clear last-updated timestamps and optionally version notes so users know currency of the data; record update history for transparency.
